analysis.title: FOMC Pre / Macro Assets & Hiking Cycles / Luxury / GTT (up) / Reckitt / Saint Gobain / BNP / Novartis / Talanx / Europe Biotech
key_insights: October FOMC preview: comments from FOMC participants since the last meeting point to a compromise of raising the funds rate every other meeting. The FOMC is set to skip a hike in October and is likely to deliver a second hike in December.

Market pricing of the Fed path has removed one hike and now peaks at just over 4.5%. GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are considerably less hawkish, because GS is skeptical the FOMC will hike four times and expects cuts down the road.
Macro assets in Fed hiking cycles: a baseline of a modest number of hikes, growth around potential and gradual inflation relief points to a modestly positive path for equities.

History points to three risk scenarios for equities. An earlier end to tightening on better inflation news would be the most positive for risk assets. An interruption driven by growth or financial stress concerns would at least initially be less friendly. A more extended tightening cycle with resilient growth could raise the risk of a larger growth downgrade later.
European luxury after 3Q26: China macro has hit hard, but the exit rate was better than in July-August. GS thinks this bodes well for the Holiday season.

GTT upgraded to Buy from Neutral with a EUR 210 12-month price target (c.16% upside) after a c.12% post-results share price drop. GTT is the global leader in LNG containment systems with an asset-light licensing model and near-100% market share at major Asian shipyards.

Reckitt core Q3 organic sales growth was +3.3% vs consensus +4.1%. Reported sales were in line. The miss came from the US, where Lysol (c.35% of US sales) had unexpected manufacturing constraints. Rated Buy.
Reckitt trades on 14.5x CY27E P/E, a 19% discount to the GS Staples sector vs parity historically.

Saint-Gobain 3Q26 organic growth was +2.5%, vs VA consensus +2.7% and GSe +3.0%, and down from +3.5% in 2Q as volumes weakened, particularly in France. FY26 EBITDA margin guidance was maintained at above 15%. Rated Neutral.
BNP Paribas Q3'26 first look: results were strong despite a weaker Arval. A new share buyback was announced and GS sees a path to additional excess capital return at year-end.

BNP Q3 revenues were c.3% above expectations, led by CIB (Equities c.30% above, FICC 2% below). Retail Banking was 2% below, driven by Arval (c.24% miss on used-car price pressure). Opex was in line and pre-provision profit was 4% above.

Novartis 3Q26 profit beat was driven by cost control. 12-month target prices are unchanged at CHF 113 / ADR $136. The stock trades near all-time highs at a c.7% premium to the sector on 2027E P/E despite significant patent expiration risk, and GS stays Sell.
The note also lists a Talanx 3Q26 earnings preview and a preview of 3Q26 for commercial SMID cap European biotech, with no detail in the text.
